theme: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS

candidates.name: smitkiri/schengen-visa
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed Schengen visa statistics by consulate: 2017-consulates-schengen-visa-stats.xlsx (638KB) and 2017-data-for-consulates.csv (156KB), plus 2018 xlsx. Consulate-level visa application/issuance/refusal counts sourced from the EU Schengen visa statistics releases. Only 2017-2018 vintages present; 0 stars, last updated 2020, no explicit license.
candidates.why_useful: Schengen visa issuance by consulate/nationality is a proxy for EU-bound inbound long-haul travel demand (EMEA region mix, gap area not directly listed but adjacent to gap #7/#10 travel volume series); dataset is old (2017-18) so mainly useful as a template for pulling the current EU Schengen visa statistics release (published annually by the European Commission) rather than as current data.

candidates.name: ilyankou/passport-index-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: 313-star, actively maintained (updated 29 Aug 2026) repo with CSVs of visa requirements for 199 countries, 2019-2025 vintages, MIT licensed. Includes a passport-index-matrix.csv (bilateral visa-requirement matrix: visa-free / visa-on-arrival / e-visa / visa-required codes between every pair of countries) and passport-index-tidy.csv, refreshed periodically from the Passport Index / Henley-style source.
candidates.why_useful: A time-stamped, versioned visa-requirement matrix lets you build a cross-border 'ease of travel' index by origin country, useful as a slow-moving control variable for APAC/LatAm inbound demand shifts (gap #7) and as a covariate in any cross-border share model (gap #20); MIT license and multi-year vintages (2019-2025) make it usable point-in-time if commit history is walked.
candidates.size_hint: multiple CSVs, low MB, 199x199 country matrix per year

candidates.name: alsonpr/Henley-Passport-Index-Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper + structured CSV output built from the Henley Passport Index API (18 stars, updated 13 Jul 2026); converts Henley's ranking/visa-free-count data per country into CSV.
candidates.why_useful: Henley Passport Index ranks countries by visa-free destination count; as a time series (if run repeatedly) it is a slow macro proxy for outbound travel friction by nationality, marginal relevance to cross-border demand splits (gap #7).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps ilyankou/passport-index-dataset conceptually but different source/format

candidates.name: alsonpr/Passport-Index-Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: 8-star repo scraping visa requirement data from 'Passport Power Index' into structured format (country pairs, visa status).
candidates.why_useful: Alternate-source passport/visa requirement dataset; redundant with ilyankou's more popular repo but confirms multiple independent sources exist for this data type.

candidates.name: rand-net/visa-cli
candidates.what_it_holds: 24-star Python CLI tool (updated 13 Sep 2026, MIT) that queries the ilyankou/passport-index-dataset to look up visa requirements between any two countries; a thin client, not a new dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the ilyankou dataset is actively used/maintained (recency signal); the CLI itself has no independent data value beyond that pointer.

candidates.name: hardikgw/cbp-wait-times
candidates.what_it_holds: Old (last commit 2016) app/pipeline that indexes CBP (US Customs and Border Protection) land-port and airport wait times into Elasticsearch. Contains app/ and conf/ directories (pipeline code), not a static committed dataset -- CBP publishes live wait times via bwt.cbp.gov XML feed which this scrapes/indexes.
candidates.why_useful: Demonstrates a working method to pull CBP border wait-time data (a real-time congestion/traffic proxy for land-border crossing volume, relevant to gap #10 border crossings), but the code is stale (2016) and would need rewriting against the current CBP feed; no historical data is stored in the repo itself.

candidates.name: EliseoCab/brownsville-wait-times
candidates.what_it_holds: Very fresh repo (last push 14 Sep 2026, same day as this scout) with committed XML snapshots of CBP Brownsville, TX Port of Entry wait times: data/bwt-all.xml (181KB, appears to be an accumulating historical log) and data/bwt.xml (3.3KB, latest snapshot), pulled from the public CBP Border Wait Times feed (bwt.cbp.gov).
candidates.why_useful: A single-port but actually time-stamped, accumulating CBP wait-time archive -- if bwt-all.xml is a running log it could give a real point-in-time series of land-border congestion (US-Mexico), a genuine proxy for cross-border travel volume (gap #10); worth checking XML contents/date range before relying on it, single port limits usefulness for a national picture.
candidates.time_coverage: unclear -- appears to be actively growing as of Sep 2026

candidates.name: Joy-Pyne/Border_Crossing_Entry_Data
candidates.what_it_holds: 14-star notebook (Joy main.ipynb, 1.2MB) analysing the BTS/data.gov 'Border Crossing Entry Data' dataset (monthly US land-border crossings by port, state, measure -- pedestrians, personal vehicles, trucks, buses, trains -- for the US-Canada and US-Mexico borders, back to 1996, at data.bts.gov/Research-and-Statistics/Border-Crossing-Entry-Data/keg4-3bc2). Repo itself is a notebook, not a raw data mirror; the underlying dataset lives at the BTS/data.gov URL.
candidates.why_useful: Points directly to the official BTS Border Crossing Entry Data API/download (monthly, 1996-present, all US land ports, mode-level detail), which is a genuine and currently free national-level cross-border volume series relevant to gap #10; better to pull straight from data.bts.gov than via this notebook, but this and ~15 nearly-identical student repos (jiy15, GauravSingh7400, dipankar9794, TejPotu, etc. -- all re-analyzing the same data.gov dataset) confirm the source and its stable Socrata endpoint id (keg4-3bc2).
candidates.size_hint: source dataset is a multi-hundred-thousand-row Socrata table; this repo just has a notebook
candidates.geography: US land border ports (Canada and Mexico borders)

queries_run: gh search repos "schengen visa statistics" --sort stars
gh search repos "border crossing entry data BTS" --sort stars
gh search repos "cbp wait times" --sort stars
gh search repos "passport index dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "border crossing entry data" --sort stars
gh search repos "TranStats border crossing" --sort updated
gh search repos "digital nomad visa dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "Schengen visa applications dataset" --sort stars
notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: no repos found at all for ESTA, ETIAS, ETIAS API mirrors, EU DAC7-adjacent visa data, or genuinely current Schengen visa application statistics (the European Commission publishes these as annual PDF/Excel releases on home-affairs.ec.europa.eu, not mirrored on GitHub as far as searched). CBP wait times exist as a live XML feed (bwt.cbp.gov) with only stale (2016) or single-port (Brownsville, fresh but narrow) GitHub captures -- no national historical archive of CBP wait times was found on GitHub; if this matters, a scraper against the live feed would need to be built fresh rather than reused. Passport-index / visa-requirement matrices (ilyankou's, 313 stars, MIT, 2019-2025, actively maintained) are the strongest find in this theme -- genuinely useful as a slow-moving cross-border friction covariate, though its relevance to ABNB nights/ADR forecasting is indirect (structural not cyclical). BTS Border Crossing Entry Data (US land-border monthly volumes since 1996) is a real, current, free, national-level cross-border travel series (gap #10) but lives at data.bts.gov / Socrata, not committed as raw data in any of the ~25 GitHub repos found -- those are all near-identical student EDA notebooks re-analysing the same data.gov pull (the excluded-pattern caveat in CONTEXT.md is about the NYC Airbnb Kaggle file specifically, but the same dynamic applies here: cite the official BTS/data.gov source directly rather than any one of these notebooks). Did not find anything on Schengen short-stay visa refusal rates by nationality/consulate more recent than 2018, ETIAS (not yet fully live as of search), or a border-crossing dataset for non-US borders (EU external border, UK, Canada-only). Suggest a future scout try 'site:github.com schengen visa refusal rate 2024 2025' via WebSearch, and check if Eurostat's migr_resvago / migr_visav visa-statistics API has a GitHub client wrapper (not found in this pass).
